_about: Short usage notes shown with a function's signature in the plugin's reference block (python/vex_function_index.py): argument order, special argument values and return conventions that the one-line help summary does not say. Hand-written; facts were taken from the Houdini help or measured in Houdini (scratch/vexlab.py). AI_WRANGLE_FUNCTION_NOTES=0 leaves them out.
invlerp: a is the value to locate: invlerp(value, min, max) = (value - min) / (max - min), not clamped.
smooth: value1 and value2 are the limits and amount is the value to test: 0 at or below value1, 1 at or above value2.
lerp: amount 0 gives value1, amount 1 gives value2.
fit: the input is clamped to omin..omax (efit does not clamp).
efit: like fit, but values outside omin..omax are extrapolated instead of clamped.
fit01: the input is taken as 0..1 and clamped.
fit10: value 1 maps to nmin and value 0 maps to nmax.
clamp: the value comes first, then min, then max.
re_replace: the regular expression comes first, then the replacement, then the string to work on.
re_find: the regular expression comes first, then the string; store the result in a typed string variable to get the matched text.
re_findall: the regular expression comes first, then the string; returns a string array.
re_match: the regular expression comes first, then the string; 1 only if the whole string matches.
re_split: the regular expression comes first, then the string.
match: the wildcard pattern (* and ?) comes first, then the string to test.
replace: returns the changed string: replace(str, old, new).
replace_match: the string comes first, then the pattern to match, then the pattern to write; * in the second pattern stands for the text that * matched in the first.
find: the string or array to search comes first, then what to look for; a negative result means not found.
split: returns a string array; the optional second argument lists the separator characters.
join: the string array comes first, then the text to put between the entries.
startswith: the string to test comes first, then the prefix.
endswith: the string to test comes first, then the suffix.
qrotate: the quaternion comes first, then the vector to rotate.
qmultiply: returns the combined rotation q1 * q2.
quaternion: the angle is in radians: quaternion(angle, axis); a matrix3 can be converted directly.
eulertoquaternion: the rotations are in radians; order is a constant such as XFORM_XYZ.
quaterniontoeuler: returns radians; order is a constant such as XFORM_XYZ.
rotate: changes the matrix in place and returns nothing; the angle is in radians.
scale: changes the matrix in place and returns nothing.
translate: changes the matrix in place and returns nothing.
prerotate: changes the matrix in place; the rotation is applied before the existing transform (in its local space); the angle is in radians.
prescale: changes the matrix in place; the scale is applied before the existing transform (in its local space).
pretranslate: changes the matrix in place; the offset is applied before the existing transform (along its local axes).
dihedral: the rotation that turns direction a onto direction b; assign it to a matrix3 or to a vector4 (quaternion).
removeprim: andpoints = 1 also deletes the points that only this primitive used; 0 keeps them.
setpointgroup: value 1 puts the point into the group, 0 takes it out.
setprimgroup: value 1 puts the primitive into the group, 0 takes it out.
setvertexgroup: value 1 puts the vertex into the group, 0 takes it out.
setdetailattrib: mode can be "set", "add", "min", "max" or "mult" for numbers, or "append" to add to a string or an array attribute (on a plain number "append" does nothing).
setpointattrib: mode can be "set", "add", "min", "max" or "mult" for numbers, or "append" to add to a string or an array attribute (on a plain number "append" does nothing).
setprimattrib: mode can be "set", "add", "min", "max" or "mult" for numbers, or "append" to add to a string or an array attribute (on a plain number "append" does nothing).
setvertexattrib: the vertex is given as a primitive number and a corner index, or as a linear vertex number with -1 as the second number.
setprimintrinsic: writable intrinsics include "closed" (open or close a curve) and "transform" (packed primitives).
surfacedist: distance_metric is "edge" or "surface"; P_attribute is usually "P"; closest_pt receives the nearest point of the group.
spline: basis is "linear", "catmull-rom", "bezier", "bspline" or "hermite"; sample_pos runs from 0 to 1.
cracktransform: c = 0 gives the translation, 1 the rotation in degrees, 2 the scale, 3 the shear; trs and xyz are constants such as XFORM_SRT and XFORM_XYZ; cast a matrix3 with (matrix).
setattrib: attribclass is "point", "prim", "vertex" or "detail"; vertex_num is only used for vertices (pass 0 otherwise).
getattrib: attribclass is "point", "prim", "vertex" or "detail"; success is set to 1 when the attribute exists.
attribtype: attribclass is "point", "prim", "vertex" or "detail"; returns 0 for integer, 1 for float, 2 for string, -1 if the attribute is missing.
attribsize: attribclass is "point", "prim", "vertex" or "detail"; 3 for a vector, 1 for a float.
attribclass: returns "point", "prim", "vertex" or "detail" (an empty string if there is no such attribute).
findattribval: attribclass is "point", "prim" or "vertex"; returns -1 if no element has the value; store the result in a typed int before using it in another call.
uniquevals: attribclass is "point", "prim", "vertex" or "detail"; assign the result to a typed int[] or string[] variable.
uniqueval: attribclass is "point", "prim", "vertex" or "detail"; which runs from 0 to nuniqueval - 1.
addprim: type is "poly" (closed polygon), "polyline" (open curve), "tet", "sphere", "circle", "tube" or "metaball"; returns the new primitive number.
addvertex: adds a corner to an existing primitive: addvertex(geohandle, prim_num, point_num).
pcfind: Pchannel is the name of the position attribute, usually "P"; returns point numbers, nearest first.
pcopen: for geometry inputs the first argument is the input number: pcopen(0, "P", position, radius, maxpoints); close the handle with pcclose.
pcimport: value is an output argument; the channel "point.distance" gives the distance to the query position.
nearpoint: returns -1 if no point lies within maxdist.
intersect: returns the number of the primitive that was hit, or -1; the length of dir is the maximum ray length; p, u and v are outputs.
intersect_all: pos, prim and uvw are output arrays; returns the number of hits.
xyzdist: prim and uv receive the closest primitive and the position on it: read attributes there with primuv(geometry, name, prim, uv).
primuv: uvw is the parametric position on the primitive, for example from xyzdist; on a quad {0.5, 0.5, 0} is the centre, on a triangle the centre is about {0.333, 0.333, 0}; {u, 0, 0} is a position along a curve.
prim_normal: uvw is the position on the primitive: on a quad {0.5, 0.5, 0} is the centre, on a triangle use about {0.333, 0.333, 0}.
minpos: returns the closest position on the surface of the given geometry.
volumesample: the second argument is the number of the volume primitive or its name, for example 0 or "density".
volumesamplev: samples a vector volume stored as three scalar volumes named like vel.x, vel.y, vel.z: pass the name without the suffix, volumesamplev(0, "vel", P). A primitive number samples only that one scalar volume and repeats it in x, y and z.
volumegradient: the second argument is the number of the volume primitive or its name; normalise the result to get a direction.
getbbox: min and max are output arguments.
relbbox: each component runs from 0 at the minimum of the bounding box to 1 at its maximum.
neighbour: returns -1 when the point has no neighbour with that index.
neighbours: returns the numbers of the points connected to the point by an edge.
sample_direction_cone: maxangle is in radians; u is a vector2 of uniform random numbers in 0..1.
sample_discrete: u is a uniform random number in 0..1; returns an index.
sample_cdf: u is a uniform random number in 0..1; returns the index whose interval of the cumulative distribution contains it.
sample_sphere_uniform: u is a vector of three uniform random numbers in 0..1; the result lies inside the unit sphere.
sample_circle_uniform: u is a vector2 of uniform random numbers in 0..1; the result lies inside the unit circle.
sample_direction_uniform: u is a vector2 of uniform random numbers in 0..1; the result is a unit vector.
sample_orientation_uniform: u is a vector of three uniform random numbers in 0..1; the result is a unit quaternion.
sample_normal: u is a uniform random number in 0..1.
sample_exponential: the mean comes first, then a uniform random number in 0..1.
rand: returns values in 0..1; assign the result to a typed variable (float or vector) to choose the overload.
noise: returns values in about 0..1; assign the result to a float or to a vector.
chramp: ramppos runs from 0 to 1; assign the result to a float for a float ramp or to a vector for a colour ramp.
argsort: returns the indices that put the array into ascending order; apply them with reorder(values, indices).
reorder: the values come first, then the array of indices.
slice: end is exclusive; negative indices count from the end.
insert: changes the array in place: insert(array, index, value).
removeindex: changes the array in place and returns the removed item.
removevalue: changes the array in place and returns 1 if the value was found.
solvequadratic: solves a t^2 + b t + c = 0; returns the number of real roots; t1 and t2 are outputs with t1 <= t2.
makebasis: xaxis and yaxis are outputs; zaxis is the given direction.
detailattrib: the third argument is ignored (pass 0); success is set to 1 when the attribute exists and 0 otherwise.
pointattrib: success is set to 1 when the attribute exists and 0 otherwise.
primattrib: success is set to 1 when the attribute exists and 0 otherwise.
vertexattrib: success is set to 1 when the attribute exists and 0 otherwise.
rgbtohsv: the hue is returned in 0..1 (not in degrees).
hsvtorgb: the hue is expected in 0..1 (not in degrees).
primvertex: converts a primitive number and a corner index into a linear vertex number.
vertexindex: converts a primitive number and a corner index into a linear vertex number.
vertexprimindex: returns the corner index of a linear vertex within its primitive.
hedge_nextequiv: returns the half-edge itself when no other face shares the edge (a boundary edge).
pointedge: returns -1 when the two points are not connected by an edge.
instance: the Z axis of the transform is aimed along N and its origin is placed at P.
getcomp: indices start at 0 (0 = x, 1 = y, 2 = z).
setcomp: changes the vector in place; the value comes before the index; indices start at 0.
lspline: sample_pos runs from 0 to 1 over the evenly spaced values.
cspline: t runs from 0 to 1; with four or more values the first and the last only shape the ends (repeat an end value to make the curve reach it); with exactly three values the curve passes through all three.
lkspline: after sample_pos the arguments come in pairs: a value, then its key position.
ckspline: after t the arguments come in pairs: a value, then its key position.
windingnumber: about 1 for a position inside a closed mesh and about 0 outside.
error: takes a printf-style format string; the node stops with this message.
warning: takes a printf-style format string; the node keeps cooking.
sprintf: %d for integers, %g for floats, %s for strings, %03d pads with zeros.
itoa: a string plus an integer does not compile ("a" + 3): convert the integer with itoa(3) or use sprintf.
noised: the first output is the noise value, the following ones its derivatives; with a vector position there are three derivative outputs (x, y, z).
mwnoise: same arguments as wnoise: the position, then outputs for the cell seed and the distances to the two nearest cell points.
cwnoise: same arguments as wnoise: the position, then outputs for the cell seed and the distances to the two nearest cell points.
wnoise: seed, dist1 and dist2 are outputs: the id of the nearest cell and the distances to the two nearest cell points.
expandpointgroup: accepts a group name or a pattern such as "0-10:2"; returns the point numbers.
expandprimgroup: accepts a group name or a pattern such as "0-10:2"; returns the primitive numbers.
polyneighbours: returns the numbers of the polygons that share an edge with the polygon.
pointprims: returns the numbers of the primitives that use the point.
primpoints: returns the point numbers of the primitive in vertex order.
packedtransform: applies the transform to the packed primitive about the origin (its position moves too).
random_ihash: the result can be negative; hash % n is still in 0 .. n - 1 because the VEX modulo is never negative.
create_cdf: takes weights (they need not sum to 1) and returns their running totals.
hscript_rand: returns exactly what the HScript expression rand() returns for the same seed.
primvertexcount: the number of vertices (corners) of the primitive.
